primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome due to COL3A1
mechanism: Pathogenic COL3A1 variants alter type III procollagen, an important structural component of skin, blood vessels, and hollow organs, causing tissue fragility and predisposition to spontaneous arterial or organ rupture.
vignette: A young adult has thin translucent skin, easy bruising, characteristic facial features, and a family history of sudden death from spontaneous arterial rupture. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic variant in COL3A1.
lead: Which of the following structural proteins is primarily affected in this disorder?
distractor_notes: Type I collagen is prominently affected in osteogenesis imperfecta and some other connective-tissue disorders, but COL3A1 encodes type III collagen.
Type IV collagen is a major basement-membrane network protein and is implicated in disorders such as Alport syndrome.
Type VII collagen forms anchoring fibrils at the dermal-epidermal junction and is implicated in dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa.
Fibrillin-1 is a microfibrillar protein affected in Marfan syndrome, not vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
key_expl: COL3A1 encodes the alpha-1 chain of type III procollagen. Type III collagen is an important structural component of skin, blood vessels, and hollow organs. Structural defects or reduced production cause the characteristic tissue fragility and high risk of arterial and organ rupture in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
objective: Identify type III collagen as the COL3A1-encoded structural protein affected in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
